recent_posts.title: Vulkan SC SDK Released: An Integrated Toolchain for Vulkan Safety-Critical Development
recent_posts.summary: The Khronos Group has released the Vulkan SC SDK (v1.0.21), a unified installer for Linux and Windows that bundles all tools needed for Vulkan Safety-Critical application development. Developed over three years by RasterGrid with Vulkan SC Working Group support, the SDK includes the Vulkan SC Loader, Emulation driver stack, Validation Layers, Device Simulation Layer, pipeline cache utilities, a sample application, and CMake integration. The goal is to reduce setup friction by replacing manual downloads and configuration with a single cohesive toolchain.

recent_posts.title: OpenCL 3.1 is Here
recent_posts.summary: Khronos has released OpenCL 3.1, the first major update to the cross-platform heterogeneous compute specification in several years. The headline change is mandatory SPIR-V ingestion across all conformant implementations, removing the last barrier for higher-level frameworks like SYCL and chipStar to fully commit to OpenCL as a runtime. Other mandated additions include subgroup operations with shuffles and rotations, integer dot products for AI inference workloads, a suggested local work-group size query, and a standard device UUID query matching Vulkan's. Several developer ergonomics improvements are also included: cleaner kernel code without extension guards, printf z/t format modifiers, clarified unified memory semantics, and a relaxed memory model scope rule. Implementations are in progress from Arm, Imagination, Intel, Mesa, and Qualcomm, plus open-source runtimes Rusticl, PoCL, and CLVK. The roadmap includes Command Buffers, Unified Shared Memory, Cooperative Matrix operations, and new low-precision AI data types.

recent_posts.title: OpenCL Cooperative Matrix Extensions Are Here
recent_posts.summary: The OpenCL Working Group has published a draft extension (cl_khr_cooperative_matrix) that brings cooperative matrix operations to OpenCL, developed with Arm, Intel, and Qualcomm. Cooperative matrix ops allow sub-groups of work-items to jointly load, multiply, and accumulate matrix tiles, mapping directly onto hardware matrix acceleration units for ML inference. The extension enables OpenCL implementations to accept SPIR-V modules using SPV_KHR_cooperative_matrix, with a new device query API for supported matrix sizes and types. A companion extension to expose these capabilities in OpenCL C (without hand-authored SPIR-V) is also in progress, with a clang frontend RFC published on LLVM Discourse. Both drafts are open for community feedback before finalization.

recent_posts.title: New OpenVX Extensions Streamline Compute Workloads on Heterogeneous SoCs
recent_posts.summary: The Khronos Group has published two new OpenVX extensions — Target Kernel and Node Command — that address key challenges in heterogeneous SoC computing. The Node Command extension introduces an asynchronous control channel separate from the data path, enabling runtime reconfiguration of vision pipelines (e.g., changing thresholds or priorities) without stopping processing or adding per-frame overhead. The Target Kernel extension allows user-defined kernels to execute directly on remote compute targets like DSPs, GPUs, and NPUs rather than being forced onto the host CPU, reducing latency and freeing the host for orchestration. Both extensions are slated to become core features in the upcoming OpenVX 2.0 release, targeting automotive, industrial robotics, and smart city use cases.

recent_posts.title: Khronos Adds Middleware Insights to the OpenXR Extension Matrix
recent_posts.summary: The Khronos OpenXR working group has expanded its Extension Matrix to include self-reported data from middleware providers, giving developers clearer visibility into which OpenXR extensions are supported across the XR stack. The updated matrix launches with five middleware components: Godot Engine, LÖVR, StereoKit, Unity, and Unreal Engine. Each cell includes clickable labels for detailed extension support information. Middleware and engine providers are invited to submit their extension support data to the working group for inclusion.

recent_posts.title: From Specification to Practice: Unlocking glTF’s Full Potential
recent_posts.summary: The Khronos 3D Formats Working Group has launched an Education, Insights, and Outreach (EIO) Subgroup to help developers and creators better use glTF and KTX in real-world workflows. The initiative addresses a persistent gap between the glTF specification and practical deployment across industries like digital twins, spatial computing, and e-commerce. The subgroup will produce tutorials, technical blogs, videos, webinars, and gather community feedback to feed back into the standardization process. A first public webinar on Gaussian splatting in glTF is scheduled for April 7, 2026, featuring speakers from Cesium, XGRIDS, and the Smithsonian covering production pipelines and real-world use cases.

recent_posts.title: Video Encoding and Decoding with Vulkan Compute Shaders in FFmpeg
recent_posts.summary: FFmpeg now uses Vulkan Compute shaders to implement fully GPU-resident video codec acceleration — covering FFv1, ProRes, ProRes RAW, and DPX in the FFmpeg 8.1 release, with VC-2, JPEG, and APV in progress. The post explains why hybrid CPU/GPU approaches historically failed (round-trip latency), how each codec's serial vs. parallel structure is tackled in compute shaders, and why Vulkan's portability and expanding feature set make it preferable to vendor-specific compute APIs. The approach complements Vulkan Video's fixed-function hardware decoders, extending GPU acceleration to professional formats and workflows those ASICs don't cover.

recent_posts.title: Khronos at 25: Shaping Visual Computing with Open Standards
recent_posts.summary: The Khronos Group celebrates 25 years of developing open standards for visual computing. Founded in 2000 by graphics and computing pioneers, Khronos created industry-defining APIs including OpenGL ES for mobile 3D graphics, WebGL for browser-based 3D, glTF for 3D asset transmission, OpenCL and SYCL for parallel computing, SPIR-V as a portable GPU intermediate representation, Vulkan for low-level GPU control, OpenXR for cross-platform XR development, and Slang for modern shader programming with AI integration. These standards enabled the evolution from desktop workstations to mobile devices, web browsers, and spatial computing platforms by providing open, interoperable foundations that connect software to hardware across vendors.

recent_posts.title: Open standards, OpenXR, and European pathways to global XR interoperability
recent_posts.summary: OpenXR is the leading open standard for XR runtimes, developed by the Khronos Group. European entities in EU-funded projects (Horizon Europe, Digital Europe) can contribute to OpenXR through consortium partners who become Khronos members, not directly as projects. Contributions include identifying gaps, prototyping extensions, providing validation results, and sharing implementation insights. Key challenges involve managing IP rights, confidentiality obligations, and patent licensing under the Khronos IP Framework. The guide outlines practical pathways for engagement across upcoming Horizon Europe calls focused on Virtual Worlds and Web 4.0, emphasizing that meaningful contribution often takes the form of requirements, architectural insights, and implementation experience rather than direct specification writing.

recent_posts.title: Khronos Announces glTF Gaussian Splatting Extension
recent_posts.summary: The Khronos Group released a candidate specification for KHR_gaussian_splatting, a glTF 2.0 extension that enables storing 3D Gaussian splats in the widely adopted glTF format. Gaussian splatting converts 2D images into photorealistic 3D assets using optimized point clouds, proving valuable for geospatial capture, digital twins, and real-time rendering. The extension allows Gaussian splats to coexist with traditional mesh-based assets while remaining algorithm-agnostic and extensible for future innovations in compression and rendering techniques. Industry stakeholders including Cesium, Esri, Niantic Spatial, and NVIDIA contributed to the specification, with ratification expected in Q2 2026 following community feedback.

top_posts.title: Ultra Engine 0.9.7 Released
top_posts.summary: Ultra Engine 0.9.7 introduces a new decals system, particle emitters, and enhanced entity and material properties. It also includes upgraded flowgraphs, over 30 bug fixes, and various improvements to compatibility and functionality. The update aims to enhance performance and visuals for game and simulation development.

top_posts.title: glTF: Now and Next
top_posts.summary: glTF has significantly evolved as a 3D format, becoming an ISO standard and integrating with various industry standards. The Khronos 3D Formats Working Group has made strides in developing new extensions for spatial computing, material rendering, and interoperability. Notable updates include improved PBR material extensions and new tools for visual consistency. Khronos continues to invite community feedback and collaboration to further enhance the glTF ecosystem.

top_posts.title: Vulkan Hardware Database by Sascha Willems
top_posts.summary: The Vulkan Hardware Database is a project managed by Sascha Willems that focuses on providing data on Vulkan-compatible hardware. The data is available under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International License, and Vulkan along with its logo are trademarks of the Khronos Group Inc.

top_posts.title: Ultra Engine 0.9.8 Adds Material Painting, Tessellation, and a First-person Shooter Template
top_posts.summary: Ultra Engine 0.9.8 introduces a new material painting system, practical tessellation features, and a first-person shooter template. These enhancements make game and simulation creation more efficient, allowing developers to create detailed, lifelike environments and realistic 3D surfaces with ease.

top_posts.title: Neural Graphics: From First Principles to Performance
top_posts.summary: The post explains how to optimize a naive gaussian splatting implementation for real-time performance, focusing on workgroup-level collaboration and memory management. It discusses breaking the process into tiles and using GPU threads for efficient computation. Further, it explores combining automatic differentiation with manual optimization strategies to reduce computational overhead and improve image quality.
